Iran offered to reopen Hormuz in a week. Trump said no.

Plus: Tigray's fighters push into Afar, Yemen's calm breaks, Serbia's president quits to run for PM, and Taiwan goes unmentioned at the Trump–Xi summit.

Five map stories, a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Iran proposed a 7-day plan: reopen the Strait of Hormuz and revive nuclear talks if the US lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump rejected it. Tehran says no official "no" has arrived. Brent topped $107.

(BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, DW, NYT)

2/ Tigrayan fighters have pushed into Ethiopia's Afar and Amhara regions and formed a new alliance to topple PM Abiy Ahmed.

Addis accuses Sudan and Egypt of backing them; Sudan's army denies it.

Afar is Ethiopia's corridor to the sea.

(Guardian, Al Jazeera)

3/ Renewed Houthi vs Saudi-backed fighting has broken four years of relative calm in Yemen, displacing families in Taiz.

Saudi Arabia's grand mufti calls the fight a religious duty; France is sending troops to guard Saudi energy sites.

(BBC, Guardian, NYT)

4/ Serbia's Aleksandar Vučić has resigned as president. Barred from a third term, he'll lead his party into early parliamentary elections next month, aiming for PM.

It follows nearly two years of student-led protests over alleged corruption.

(BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera, NYT)

5/ At the Trump–Xi summit, trade and AI filled the public talk. Taiwan was discussed only in private.

Xi pressed on US support for Taiwan and Japan. The US ambassador says Trump even asked if China wanted to buy US weapons.

(BBC, Guardian, DW, NYT)

The data behind it: oil production, 2024.

Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran and the UAE form one dense cluster, and most of their exports leave by sea through one ~40km gap: Hormuz. Saudi's main bypass ends on the Red Sea, now under Houthi fire.
